appliance_run_value_tooltip: Which value of the status means that a programme is running. Without it every word that does not mean standing still counts as running.
button_release_tooltip: For a relay that is wired as a pulse: this is written a moment after the first value. Leave it empty for anything else.
button_value_tooltip: Empty means `true`. A number is written as a number, everything else as text.
camera_oid_tooltip: A state that carries the address, or the picture itself as `data:image/...`. It wins over the fixed address.
chart_no_history: This state is not recorded. Switch on a history adapter for it, then the chart has something to draw.
chart_smoothing_tooltip: A meter that is read every ten seconds draws a saw, and the saw says nothing that the shape underneath it does not say better. Each reading is replaced by the average around it, so the line stays where it is.
chart_spline_tooltip: The readings are joined by a curve instead of by straight lines. The curve never leaves the range between two readings, so a value that never fell below zero is not drawn dipping under it.
chart_step_tooltip: Draw it as a step curve: the value holds until the next one arrives. That is how a switch behaves, and how a set temperature behaves.
dimmer_on_behaviour_tooltip: Only for a lamp without a state of its own for on and off. Such a lamp goes out by being set to nothing, and nothing is all that is left of where it stood.
help_appliance: The one device in the house that is looked at for a single reason: whether it is done yet. The ring says how far the programme has got, the middle how much longer it has, and underneath stands the time of day it will be finished at. Every state is optional but the status - a machine that only reports the remaining minutes gets a turning drum instead of a ring.
help_blind: A blind with the window it hangs in: pull it with the mouse, or use up, stop and down. It shows the number the state carries, which in ioBroker is how much light comes in.
help_button: Something happens when it is pressed, and nothing is shown afterwards: a scene, a script, a doorbell, a gate. For a relay wired as a pulse it can write a second value a moment later, which saves a script that exists only for that. It can ask before it fires, and ask for a PIN.
help_camera: The picture a camera takes: from the cameras adapter, from a doorbell over HTTP, or straight out of a state that carries it. A still picture has to be fetched again to stay a picture of now, which is what the interval is for. On a floor plan the camera is a dot — the click opens the card, and that is where the picture is.
help_chart: What a value did, as a card of its own: two states against each other, a day of the heating, the power of the last week. The measured value carries its history behind its number; this is for when the course itself is the point. It draws only what a history adapter records.
help_clock: The one thing on a dashboard that is not a device. A tablet on a wall is a clock for most of the day, and one that has to be read off the corner of the system bar is no clock. With hands or in digits, with the date under it.
help_dimmer: A lamp that is more than on or off: a toggle to switch it and a slider for the brightness. Works with a scale of 0 to 100 as well as 0 to 255.
help_iframe: A web page inside a widget: a camera, a chart of another adapter, a timetable, a map. It can reload itself for pages that never update on their own. What it cannot do is reach into the page — a browser keeps a frame from another site to itself, and that is the right way round.
help_knob: Any number set by hand that is not a light: the volume, a fan speed, how far a valve is open. As a knob to read from across a room, or as a slider to save height in a list.
help_link: A card that leads somewhere: to another page of this project, or to an address of its own. A start page with a tile per room reads better than a list at the side, and on a floor plan a marker that opens the detail page of a room is the natural gesture.
help_lock: A lock: locked or not, with the door opener beside it where there is one. It asks before both ways by default — a dashboard hangs where everyone walks past it, and a front door is not something to open because a sleeve brushed the screen. A PIN can be set for it.
help_media: What is playing, and the four buttons one reaches for. Which of them a given player has is its own business - some have one state that is play and pause at once, some have a button per action - so every one of them is a field and the card shows what it was given. Where there is a cover, that is what the card is mostly made of: a title in twelve point tells you what is playing, a cover tells you across the room.
help_rgb: Colour light with a wheel, a brightness bar and - where the lamp can do it - colour temperature and a white channel. Six ways of telling a lamp a colour.
help_security: Armed, disarmed, or going off — three states and nothing else is the honest shape of it. What arming means (everybody out, or somebody asleep upstairs) is the system’s own business: where it says so in its object, the card shows those as buttons; where it does not, the buttons it was given do. Like the lock it asks on both ways by default, and a PIN can be set for it. Disarming a house from a tablet in the hall is exactly the move that should cost one.
help_sensor: A state that is only ever one of two things: a window, a door, motion, smoke, water. Say what it watches and it finds its symbol and its words; mark it as an alarm and it turns red when it goes off.
help_switch: Anything that is on or off: a socket, a lamp, a pump. The card can ask before it switches, and ask for a PIN.
help_tank: A cistern, an oil tank, a pellet store, a battery: a bar with a scale beside it, because nobody reads a fill level as a number — they read it as a height. Set a warning level and it turns red before the tank is empty.
help_text: Words that are not a device: a heading over a section, a room name on a floor plan, a note. It can carry the value of a state after its text, and it has no card around it — a heading in a frame is not a heading.
help_theme: A dashboard in a hallway is read in daylight and at night, and which theme it should be in is nothing the project can know. The switch changes the runtime itself, so every card, every marker and the menu change with it, and the choice is remembered in the browser. A view that must always be dark sets one theme instead, and one that should look like the rest of the device follows the browser.
help_thermostat: What the room is, what it should be, and what the heating is doing about it. Drag the knob along the scale; the modes come from the object, whatever the manufacturer calls them.
help_vacuum: A robot is a device one gives two orders to - go, and come back - and otherwise only looks at. What it says about itself it says in its own words, out of the object: no two manufacturers agree on them. The map some robots serve is a picture behind an address, so the camera widget shows it.
help_value: A measured value to read: temperature, humidity, power. Where the state is logged the card draws its history behind the number, shows which way it is going, and opens the chart on a click.
help_weather: What the weather is doing now, and what it will do. Every weather adapter serves the same handful of readings under a different name, so each one is a field and the card shows what it was given: with only a temperature it is a thermometer, with everything it is a weather station. The icons are the ones the adapter serves — a widget that drew its own would disagree with the forecast that comes with them.
help_window: A window or a door drawn as one: closed, tilted or standing open. The shape is recognised across a room, before anybody reads a word.
iframe_oid_tooltip: For a page whose address changes — a camera snapshot with a token, for instance. It wins over the fixed address.
inverted_tooltip: In ioBroker 100 % is open and 0 % closed. Switch this on for a device that counts the other way round.
knob_color_to_tooltip: With this the scale runs from one colour into the other, the way the thermostat runs from cold to warm. Leave it empty for a scale of one colour.
knob_ticks_tooltip: How many marks the scale carries, the two ends included. Five give the quarters; nothing at all leaves the scale plain.
link_new_window: In a tab of its own
link_url_tooltip: For somewhere outside this project: a camera’s own interface, a manual, the router.
lock_inverted_tooltip: In ioBroker a lock that reads `true` is an open one — the state says whether it lets anyone through. Switch this on for a lock that counts the other way round.
name: Name
oid_end_time_tooltip: A moment as a unix time, as a date, or simply as the time of day - 14:35 is read as today, or as tomorrow once it is past.
oid_start_time_tooltip: With the start and the end the ring shows how far the programme has got; without them the drum simply turns.
oid_value_tooltip: Its value is written after the text, which turns `Outside` into `Outside 6.4 °C`.
pin_tooltip: With a PIN the question is answered by typing it. It is kept in the project, so it keeps the wrong hand away, not the wrong person.
presets_tooltip: Separated by a semicolon: 12;18;22;24 gives four buttons. Nobody wants 21.5 degrees — they want the number they call «night» or «comfortable», and everybody in the house knows those by heart.
rgb_mode: How the lamp is told the colour
sensor_alarm_tooltip: An alarm fills its card and its marker in red instead of only colouring the ring. Whether a device is one is your judgement: a contact on the garden gate at night is an alarm, the same contact on the kitchen window in July is not.
tank_low_tooltip: Below this the card and the marker turn red — a tank is worth knowing about before it is empty, not after.
tank_value_position_tooltip: Beside the bar the number takes a third of the width, and a bar a third narrower is harder to read at a glance — which is the whole point of drawing one.
theme_mode_tooltip: As a switch it flips between the light and the dark theme of the pair the runtime is in. Fixed sets one theme when the page opens and leaves it at that; following the browser takes what the device is set to and changes with it.
tilt_value_tooltip: Only for a window that knows three positions. Where the object lists three values, the middle one is taken as tilted by itself.
